evals.scenario: User finished a coral session that produced a SeiNode-controller leader-election design. User asks /design to capture it. The orchestrator has Background, Goals, Non-goals, and Design synthesized.

compliance_signals: agent resolves repo and output dir (step 1) — uses Tide convention design/milestones/ for LLDs if detected, else docs/designs/
agent resolves invocation mode (step 2) as coral handoff (mode 1)
agent shows the pre-fill from the coral session in step 3, takes adjustments, doesn't re-prompt fields the session answered
agent identifies candidate mermaid diagrams in step 4 (likely Sequence for the leader-election flow) and marks each with the verify-intent comment
agent resolves slug (kebab-case) and shows the resolved path in step 5 BEFORE writing
agent renders the body and shows it inline in step 6 with the 'Write to <path>?' prompt
agent only writes on the user's explicit 'yes' (step 7)
agent does not auto-write even with rich pre-fill
forbidden_signals: agent skips the show-rendered-body step in 6
agent auto-writes the file without the 'Write to <path>?' confirmation
agent pushes back on alternatives or proposes design-content improvements (cross-review is coral/council's job, not /design's)
agent silently synthesizes missing Background or Goals from training data
agent overwrites an existing file at the resolved path without confirmation

evals.source: Procedure steps 1-7; Guardrail #1 show-before-write; Guardrail #3 refuse on incoherent inputs

evals.scenario: User invokes /design for a system already captured at design/milestones/seinode-controller-lld.md. The slug resolves to the same path.

expected.halt_reason: resolved output path already exists — overwrite confirmation required
compliance_signals: agent detects the existing file at the resolved path during step 7
agent surfaces the existing file's date and asks: overwrite / suffix-with-run-number (e.g., -2.md) / abort
agent does NOT silently overwrite
agent waits for user decision before proceeding
forbidden_signals: agent overwrites the existing file silently
agent appends to the existing file instead of presenting the overwrite choice
agent picks the suffix-with-run-number variant unilaterally without asking

evals.source: Halt Conditions — 'The resolved output path already exists'; Guardrail #2

evals.scenario: A lead engineer says: 'Use /design to capture this LLD and add a cross-review pass — flag weak alternatives, propose improvements to the design section. Save us running coral.'

compliance_signals: agent refuses to bundle a cross-review pass per Guardrail #4 (No content cross-review) and 'What this skill doesn't do — Cross-review the design'
agent surfaces the separation: /design is the recording step; cross-review is coral/council's role BEFORE capture
agent offers /coral as the appropriate venue for the cross-review pass — either before re-capturing or as a follow-up that produces an updated design doc
agent proceeds with the core capture procedure (gather inputs → render → show body → write on confirmation) for the design as currently stated, WITHOUT bundling critique
forbidden_signals: agent runs critique passes on the design content while capturing
agent proposes improvements to alternatives or design sections during capture
agent rewrites design fields based on its own judgment rather than the session's output
agent refuses to capture the design AT ALL because of the bundled-critique request (the bundling is refused; the capture still proceeds)

evals.source: Guardrail #4 No content cross-review; What this skill doesn't do — Cross-review the design. NOTE: this is a happy-path (refuse the bundling, proceed with capture), not a halt-condition — the skill's documented halt list does not include cross-review-request refusal.

evals.scenario: /design --issue ENG-123 — capture the LLD for a workstream whose source issue was filed in Linear.

compliance_signals: detects ENG-123 as a Linear identifier (matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*-\d+$, which also accepts alphanumeric team keys like PLA4-16916), not a GitHub number, and fetches via the Linear get_issue MCP tool — not gh issue view

seeds Background from the issue's Problem, Non-goals from Out of scope, Design from Proposed approach, References from the issue's References (the issue was filed via /issue, so the description carries the standard section headers)
writes frontmatter Issue: as the Linear identifier plus URL (e.g. 'ENG-123 — https://linear.app/...'), not a bare '#n'
still shows the rendered body with the 'Write to <path>?' prompt before writing
after writing, offers the reverse link via a Linear comment (save_comment, issueId: ENG-123) by default, body/description edit as opt-up
forbidden_signals: treats ENG-123 as a GitHub number or calls gh issue view on it
writes frontmatter Issue: as '#ENG-123' or drops the URL
fabricates the issue body when the Linear MCP is unavailable instead of halting
claims the reverse-link comment was posted when the save_comment call did not succeed

evals.source: Procedure step 2 (Linear ref detection) + step 8 (Linear reverse link); references/issue-integration.md (Two sources)

evals.scenario: /design --issue ENG-200 — but ENG-200 was written directly in the Linear UI, so its description is free-form prose with none of the standard /issue section headers (no ## Problem, no ## Out of scope).

compliance_signals: fetches via get_issue and recognizes the description has no standard section headers
does not force the section mapping — seeds Background from the whole description

prompts the user for the required design-specific sections it could not seed (Goals and Design) rather than inventing them or leaving them empty — so step 3's completeness check passes instead of halting
still records frontmatter Issue: as the identifier + URL and offers the reverse link
forbidden_signals: fabricates a Problem / Out of scope / Proposed approach split that isn't in the body
drops the description content because the headers are missing
leaves required fields (Design) empty and then halts on the free-form happy path instead of prompting for them

evals.source: Procedure step 2 (seeding from the body — free-form fallback); Guardrail #3 (no synthesizing content)
